positions.as_written: Seeing it on a plain radiograph should prompt a search for a cruciate injury rather than treatment of the fragment.
Expect a higher grade pivot shift where it is present.
Use it as evidence of an attachment region rather than of a named structure.
Treat the lesion as an indication to consider a lateral procedure, on the ground that it is direct evidence of anterolateral injury in a knee where that is otherwise inferred.
Consider a lateral procedure where the lesion is present.
Leave the fragment unfixed unless it is large and displaced.
